children: KB reported third-quarter 2026 results with revenues of $1.30 billion and diluted earnings per share of $1.05, reflecting weaker demand versus the prior year. The company repurchased $50.0 million of common stock in the quarter and said built-to-order homes accounted for nearly three-quarters of deliveries. Management noted sequential margin improvement despite ongoing affordability pressure from higher mortgage rates.
Total revenues: $1.30 billion for the three months ended August 31, 2026 (down 20% year over year).
Homebuilding operating income: $67.1 million for the quarter; homebuilding operating income margin of 5.2% (5.4% excluding inventory-related charges).
Housing gross profit margin: 16.5% for the quarter (16.8% excluding $3.0 million inventory-related charges).
Pretax income: $81.2 million for the quarter; net income: $65.3 million with an effective tax rate of 19.6%.
Diluted earnings per share: $1.05 for the quarter; nine-month diluted EPS: $2.00.
Built-to-order (BTO) strategy: BTO homes represented nearly three-quarters of deliveries in the quarter, supporting sequential margin improvement.
Community expansion: Average community count grew 8% to 279 for the quarter, ending community count rose to 277, driven by new community openings over the past year.
Backlog growth: Ending backlog homes increased 2% to 4,398 and backlog value rose 3% to $2.05 billion, the first backlog increase in four years.

Liquidity and capital allocation: Total liquidity of $942.4 million (including $159.0 million cash) and $725.0 million remaining under the current repurchase authorization after $50.0 million repurchased in the quarter.
